sections.title: The sound of oy
paragraphs: The letters oy make the diphthong in (boy) /bɔɪ/, which means a young male person. A diphthong is two vowel sounds in one syllable, where the sound glides from the first to the second. These letters have only one sound in English. You hear this sound at the end of many common words.

sections.title: Mouth shape
paragraphs: Start with your lips open and round. Pull your tongue back and low in your mouth. Voice the first part. Then glide your tongue up and forward towards the roof of your mouth. Relax your lips into a wide smile as you finish. Touch your throat with your hand to feel the strong vibration through the whole sound.

sections.title: When to use oy
paragraphs: The letters oy write the vowel sound in (toy) /tɔɪ/ everywhere they appear. You see this spelling most often at the end of a syllable or word. It always stays one smooth gliding sound.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not separate the two parts into two distinct syllables. Glide smoothly between them in one breath. Do not make the first vowel too long or flat. Start with round lips and move immediately towards a light smile.
